frozen_taxonomy_outcome.condition_met: K3 does not substantially beat K0 (headroom < 0.15 at every scale, actual 0.0-0.013)
frozen_taxonomy_outcome.prescribed_action: Endpoint semantics is not the primary problem. Reopen entity-link construction / relation attachment / path topology before touching ranking. Do not build a richer relation-semantics layer on top of this recognizer -- that was the wrong next step (Outcome C's action), and this run is what distinguishes C from D.

headline_finding.claim: K3 (the oracle ceiling, restricted to records the SAME topology walk K0/K1 already reach) barely beats K0 at all.
headline_finding.meaning: Even a PERFECT completion recognizer -- one that never mislabels a single record -- could not have closed more than 0.7-1.3 percentage points of working-set CES, because the records it would need to label correctly are usually not reachable by the graph's 1-2 hop co-mention walk in the first place. R_endpoint for K3 is 1.000 at every scale by construction (it always recognizes what it can reach); R_endpoint for K0/K1 is only 0.06-0.10. That gap looks large in isolation, but the DENOMINATOR it operates on (topology-reachable required records) is small and mostly overlaps with what K0's loose substring match already recovers through partial-tier admission -- G2 does not pad the working set, so partial (non-complete) records still enter it whenever total candidates are below M, which they almost always are here (working sets averaged 6-25 records against ceilings of 25-75).

G2_V2_RESULT.next_diagnostic_question: Why is the 1-2 hop co-mention topology so sparse relative to required evidence? Candidates: (a) the corpus's multi-hop chains route through bridges that are NOT co-mentioned with the subject in any single record (i.e. the true link is a chain of separate facts, not a shared record), (b) entity extraction (extract_v4_entities) fails to recognize the SAME entity across records due to surface-form variance, fragmenting what should be one node into several, or (c) the candidate pool depth (C2 expanded k) doesn't retrieve the specific bridge/endpoint records at all, independent of graph construction. This needs its own diagnostic pass over topology_reachable_records vs required_evidence_ids before any repair is attempted -- not assumed.
G2_V2_RESULT.stop_gate: FAILED at every scale -- no eligible M passed the frozen 0.50 construction-gap bound. decision_M=None (correctly, not 'least bad'), per the decision_at_M hard-gate fix applied in this sprint.
what_survives_from_this_sprint: hrm_adaptive_memory/c4/relation_grammar.py: a working, tested entity-bound relation parser grounded in the actual generator grammar (11/13 real corpus samples bind correctly vs 0/4 for the pre-existing relational_state.py parser on similar samples) -- reusable when topology is eventually repaired
hrm_adaptive_memory/c4/endpoint_recognition.py: K0/K1/K2 with full provenance, 72 passing tests
hrm_adaptive_memory/c4/decision_gate.py: fixes the decision_at_M hard-gate bug present in run_g1_typed_path.py and run_g2_graph_traversal.py (5 regression tests)
directed ENTITY_LINKED_TO_ENTITY edge pairs in runtime_graph.py (provenance repair)
G2_V2_RESULT.why_this_overturns_the_g2_v1_diagnosis: G2-v1 attributed the failure to completion RECOGNITION (a record wasn't being labeled complete even though it should have been). This sprint's K3 arm falsifies that: recognition was never the binding constraint. The actual constraint is REACHABILITY -- required records frequently sit outside the 1-2 hop subject/bridge co-mention neighborhood the runtime graph walks at all, so no completion rule, however accurate, can recover them. K1's entity-bound recognizer IS more correct than K0 in isolation (see tests/unit/test_g2_endpoint_recognition.py -- it correctly rejects wrong-entity bindings K0 falsely accepts, and correctly recognizes value-shaped records the older relational_state.py parser missed entirely). Being more correct did not help end-to-end because the records it could have correctly labeled were mostly unreachable to begin with.

g2_v1_diagnosis_this_sprint_repairs.finding: RECORD_EXPRESSES_RELATION was a substring match of the parsed relation phrase against raw record text -- not entity-bound. paths_enumerated and unique_bridge_entities climbed with scale, so the graph found bridges; paths_complete stayed low (1.6-3.1 of 9-39 enumerated) because completion recognition, not traversal or ranking, was the defect.
g2_v1_diagnosis_this_sprint_repairs.hypothesis_this_sprint_tests: H1: a path endpoint can instantiate the requested relation even when the exact normalized relation phrase does not appear literally in the record, via entity-bound structured parsing. H0: even oracle-correct endpoint recognition does not substantially repair G2, implying graph topology/link structure itself is insufficient.

K0_literal.definition: unchanged G2-v1 behavior -- relation_norm substring anywhere in record text, no entity binding. This is exactly runtime_graph.py's existing RECORD_EXPRESSES_RELATION signal.

K1_entity_bound.definition: entity-bound EXACT relation match. Reuses the already-frozen, already-tested hrm_adaptive_memory/c4/relational_state.py:parse_relation_edges to extract (source_entity, relation, target_entity) triples from record text via its existing template grammar (regex patterns matched against the corpus's own generator grammar -- Changelog:/Revision applied/registry entry/JSON kv/etc, all of which are visible surface forms, not oracle fields). A record completes a path for (entity, target_relation) iff some parsed RelationFact binds that specific entity (as source or target) to a relation that normalizes to an EXACT match of target_relation. This is 'record expresses relation about this bridge entity', not merely 'relation phrase occurs in record'.

K2_family_normalized.definition: identical to K1 but relation matching uses relational_state.py's existing _relation_matches (partial substring + a small frozen synonym table: assigned category<->category/assigned, ownership tier<->tier/ownership, calibration class<->calibration/class, routing class<->routing/class). This table already exists and is already covered by 19 passing tests in test_c4_relational_state.py -- K2 does NOT introduce a new alias table or config file; it reuses this exact frozen function verbatim. No alias is added because of anything observed in K1/K2 output.

K3_oracle_ceiling.definition: a record/entity pair is a correct endpoint iff the record_id is in task['required_evidence_ids'] AND the (entity, record_id) pair was ALREADY discovered by the shared K0/K1 topology pass (i.e. record_id in subject_records or in some bridge's bridge_records) -- K3 relabels completion, it does NOT add new bridges/entities/edges. Isolated in hrm_adaptive_memory/c4/oracle_endpoint_ceiling.py, evaluator-only, never imported by runtime endpoint_recognition.py or g2_paths.py.

ladder.not_run_K2_default: K2 runs only if K1 fails to close a material fraction of K3's gap; per instruction, do not let K2 become an open-ended synonym-tuning exercise.
